problem: The pricing parity recovery was merged to current GitHub main, but Netlify production remained on a parallel pricing merge and therefore served an older built artifact without the full Portal capability section.
root_cause: Concurrent pricing delivery lineages completed out of order between GitHub main and Netlify production. Commit identity alone was insufficient because Netlify's current deploy pointed to a different parallel lineage.
prevention: After a pricing recovery merge, verify Netlify current deploy is the current main commit or a descendant containing that recovery.
If a parallel deploy wins the production race, create a governed promotion successor on the current main epoch rather than accepting stale production.
Terminal pricing completion requires public content readback of the parity tokens, not only GitHub merge or Netlify ready state.

evidence.production_observation: GitHub main was 276a6d313662b59f2e73f320bcbf26de18d65719 while Netlify current deploy 6ab3844039f46f0008a4174a served commit e6a92c0341397e87a251802e951878dab0dfae2b and public /prijzen omitted the parity block.
acceptance: public /prijzen contains full Portal capability heading
